messages:
asha-gh: Quick sync — we need a decision on OTLP routing strategy for collector pipelines. Two big constraints: per-tenant retention/quota + on-prem/private customers that can't hit our central gateway. Options I see: agent-heavy (per-signal pipelines + local sampling), gateway-heavy (central routing + quota enforcement), or hybrid. Thoughts?
ryan-oc: Gateway-heavy makes enforcing quotas/simple rollouts easier (single place to patch). But it does mean more network egress from agents and a bigger SLO surface for the gateway.
ryan-oc: also we can do tenant-aware routing at gateway and fallback to local exporters for private deployments.
sophia-pl: Agent-side pipelines let teams customize quickly and reduce pressure on gateway, but they're a PITA to rollout consistently. If we adopt agent-side, we need a control-plane API to publish pipeline specs and a safe rollout UX.
kevin-infra: Agree with sophia. Private deployments can't rely on cloud gateway, so agent needs to be functional offline. However, for hosted customers, gateway-level telemetry policing (quotas, throttling, reroute to cheaper model) is valuable.
kevin-infra: Proposal: Default to agent doing lightweight preprocessing + sampling, gateway does heavy routing/enrichment/quota checks for hosted. Provide control-plane flag to pin a tenant to agent-only mode.
sophia-pl: That feels reasonable. Also: we should standardize what "lightweight preprocessing" means. I suggest: attribute extraction, basic span-level sampling (head-based), and batching/compression. No exporter transformations.
asha-gh: +1. Important: retention must be configurable per-tenant and per-signal. Example: dev teams want 7d spans, security wants 90d. We need TTL metadata with enforcement at storage/exporter side.
kevin-infra: We should propagate a retention hint on the span bundles: header like X-Redwood-Retention: 90d. Gateway/storage uses it to index into the proper bucket. But beware: that leaks policy into path — need ACL checks.
sophia-pl: For hosted GDPR customers we'll also need a delete API tied to tenant and time ranges. Put that on roadmap for private as well.
ryan-oc: Operationally, gateway can map retention->S3 lifecycle or DB tier. For on-prem, agent can write to local retention tier config and enforce TTL locally.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: config push to staging succeeds: /configs/collector/policies/1851234567 v0.3
asha-gh: Quick config sketch (for discussion):
```yaml
service_pipelines:
  spans:
    processors:
      - extract_attributes: { include: [tenant_id, env] }
      - sampling: { type: head, ratio: 0.1 }
    exporters:
      - otlp/grpc: { endpoint: gateway.internal:4317, headers: {"x-retention": "90d"} }
  metrics:
    processors:
      - batch: { timeout_ms: 200 }
    exporters:
      - prometheus_local
```
ryan-oc: That shows the hybrid model well. One more Q: throttling granularity — token-bucket per-tenant, per-signal, or both? My vote: per-tenant global + per-signal soft limits.
sophia-pl: Per-signal soft limits make sense to avoid noisy-signal storms (e.g., traces vs logs). Console should surface per-signal ingestion rate and quota burn. Dashboards: "ingest_bytes_per_tenant", "span_sample_rate", "quota_remaining".
kevin-infra: We also need an internal API for the control-plane to update sampling policies atomically and backfill a rollout plan (canary tenants, rollout percentage). UX ask: allow selecting a tenant cohort and toggling sampling or retention with a dry-run mode.
asha-gh: For canaries, prefer percent rollouts based on hashed tenant_id so it's deterministic. And always include a kill-switch that forces fallback to gateway-default pipeline.
ryan-oc: Bandwidth calc: if avg span size = 1.5KB, 100k spans/sec => ~150MB/s. Sampling at 0.1 reduces to 15MB/s. Good to show these numbers in proposal for capacity planning.
sophia-pl: Agreed. Also add OTLP-level batching/compression (gzip) into agent defaults to save bandwidth.
kevin-infra: Security note — exporters must respect tenant ACLs. Gateway should validate tenant tokens before applying retention hints.
asha-gh: Next steps: 1) ryan to draft gateway quota API + token-bucket spec; 2) sophia to design agent control-plane fetch + local enforcement; 3) kevin to write storage retention mapping doc (lifecycle rules). Sync tomorrow 10:30.
ryan-oc: I'll post an RFC later today with examples and perf numbers.
sophia-pl: I'll mock the console rollout UX (canary toggle + dry-run).
kevin-infra: I'll put retention mapping PR up to docs repo.
asha-gh: Thanks all — feel free to DM if you want to add other constraints before the RFC. :rocket:
